mainTopic: The כף and מחתה in the קטורת service, the stories of רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית, and the rules of קמיצה and חפינה
overview: The משנה describes how the כהן גדול fills a כף with handfuls of קטורת and then holds the מחתה of coals in his right hand and the כף in his left. The גמרא explains that there are two pans, one of coals and one of incense. A spoon is needed because the coals and the incense must come in together in one הבאה, and there is no respectful way to do this by hand. The coal pan goes in the right hand because it is heavier, and even when the weights are equal, because it is hot. This leads to stories about רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית: his huge handfuls, two times a brother replaced him as כהן גדול, and his mother's modesty, which the חכמים said could not fully explain her reward. Finally, the גמרא asks whether the חפינה of קטורת may be measured with a vessel, as is forbidden for the קומץ of a מנחה. Attempted proofs from 'וכך היתה מדתה' are pushed off. A ברייתא then defines a proper קומץ: three fingers closed over the palm.

steps.title: The משנה: preparing the spoon and the pan for the incense
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes how the כהן גדול fills the כף with handfuls of קטורת and then holds the מחתה in his right hand and the כף in his left.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought out to him the spoon and the pan. He scooped his handfuls and put them into the spoon. A big-handed כהן גדול scooped a big amount, and a small-handed one scooped a small amount. That was the measure. He took the pan in his right hand and the spoon in his left.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out the steps of getting the קטורת ready before the כהן גדול walks into the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of incense is not a fixed measurement. It depends on the size of this particular כהן גדול's hands. He then holds the pan of coals in his right hand and the spoon of incense in his left.

keyTerms.meaning: Spoon or ladle, a vessel used to hold the incense
He scooped with both cupped hands

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the גמרא here examines details from this משנה: the מחתה, the כף, which hand holds which vessel, and the phrase 'וכך היתה מדתה'.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹצִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַכַּף וְאֶת הַמַּחְתָּה,
phrases.english: They brought out for him the spoon and the pan,
he scooped his full handfuls
and placed them into the spoon.
phrases.notes: The incense is scooped by hand and then put into the spoon.

phrases.english: The big one, according to his bigness,
phrases.notes: A כהן גדול with large hands scoops more.

phrases.english: and the small one, according to his smallness.
And this was its measure.
He took the pan in his right hand
and the spoon in his left.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹצִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַכַּף וְאֶת הַמַּחְתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of this passage: the base משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול scoops handfuls of קטורת into a כף, sized by his own hands. He holds the מחתה in his right hand and the כף in his left.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention the pan a second time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: an earlier משנה already taught that the כהן גדול takes a מחתה, so why repeat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: A pan? The משנה already taught us: 'He took the pan, went up to the top of the altar, scooped up coals, and came down!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that the משנה brings out a מחתה, because an earlier משנה already described the כהן גדול taking a מחתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה described the כהן גדול taking a pan to collect coals from the altar. If that pan is already in his hand, bringing out a pan again seems repetitive or confusing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA. A pan?
phrases.notes: An expression of surprise.

phrases.english: He already taught it:
"He took the pan
and went up to the top of the altar
and scoops coals and comes down!"
phrases.notes: Quoted from the earlier משנה (יומא מג:).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a detail in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's mention of bringing out a מחתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מחתה was already described in an earlier משנה, so mentioning it again seems redundant.

steps.title: Two different pans: one for coals, one for incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the earlier משנה spoke of a pan of coals, while this משנה speaks of a separate pan of incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is a pan of coals, and here it is a pan of incense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining that two different pans are involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is repeated. The first pan holds burning coals from the altar. The second pan holds the supply of קטורת, which the כהן גדול scoops from into the spoon.
steps.confusionAlert: In the final line of the משנה, the מחתה held in the right hand is the pan of coals. The incense pan is only used to scoop from. Do not mix the two pans up.

phrases.english: There, it is a pan of coals,
and here, it is a pan of incense,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם מַחְתָּה דְגֶחָלִים, וְהָכָא מַחְתָּה דִקְטוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one pan exists, so the משנה is repeating itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two pans: one of coals and one of incense.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves there was a separate pan of incense
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that an empty כף came from the vessel chamber and a heaped pan of incense came from לשכת בית אבטינס.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: they brought him an empty spoon from the Chamber of Vessels, and a heaped pan of incense from the Chamber of the House of אבטינס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its answer that there was a special pan full of incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states outright that the pan brought out was heaped with קטורת. This proves the משנה's מחתה is the incense pan, not the coal pan. It also tells us the spoon arrived empty and was then filled by the כהן גדול's handfuls.

keyTerms.meaning: The family that prepared the incense, and their chamber

steps.whatToRemember: There are two pans in this service: a pan of coals from the altar, and a heaped pan of קטורת from בית אבטינס. The כף starts out empty.

phrases.english: As it was taught: They brought out for him an empty spoon
from the Chamber of Vessels,
and a pan heaped with incense
from the Chamber of the House of Avtinas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's מחתה is a pan of incense
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the pan was heaped with קטורת from לשכת בית אבטינס

steps.title: Why use a spoon if the Torah says 'his handfuls'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about filling the כף, then asks why a spoon is needed on יום הכיפורים when the פסוק says the כהן גדול brings 'his full handfuls.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: He scoops his handfuls and puts them into the spoon, the big one by his bigness and the small one by his smallness, and that was the measure. Why do I need a spoon on יום הכיפורים? The תורה said, 'his full handfuls, and he shall bring'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next part of the משנה. It then challenges the use of a spoon at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא טז:יב) seems to say the incense should be carried in the hands themselves. Putting it into a vessel looks like it goes against the plain meaning of 'his handfuls.'

phrases.aramaic: חָפַן מְלֹא חׇפְנָיו וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ הַכַּף.
phrases.english: "He scoops his full handfuls and places them into the spoon.
phrases.notes: The גמרא re-quotes the משנה to begin a new discussion.

phrases.english: The big one, according to his bigness,
and the small one, according to his smallness.
And this was its measure."
Why do I need a spoon on Yom Kippur?
"His full handfuls... and he shall bring," the Merciful One said!
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:יב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new detail of the משנה: the כף
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement to put the handfuls into a כף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'his handfuls … and he shall bring,' which implies the incense is carried by hand and not in a vessel.

steps.title: The spoon is needed because everything must be brought in one trip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no other way. The כהן גדול cannot make two trips, because the תורה requires one single act of bringing for the coals and the incense together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is impossible otherwise. What should he do? Bring one in and then bring the other in? The תורה said one bringing, not two bringings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the spoon is used out of necessity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול must carry both the pan of coals and the incense into the קודש הקדשים together. If his hands were full of incense, he could not also hold the coal pan. Two separate trips are not allowed, because the פסוק teaches a single הבאה, so the incense is carried in a spoon.
steps.whatToRemember: The כף is used because the coals and the incense must enter the קודש הקדשים in one הבאה. The handfuls still set the amount, but the spoon carries them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the פסוק's words 'his handfuls' measure the amount of incense. They do not forbid carrying it in a vessel, because a single trip is the higher requirement.

phrases.english: Because it is impossible otherwise,
for how should we do it?
Let him bring in one, and then bring in the other?
phrases.notes: First the coal pan, then the incense: two trips.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said one bringing,
and not two bringings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical necessity based on another requirement of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The incense should be carried in the bare hands, as the פסוק says 'his handfuls.'
steps.terutzMaskana: A spoon is required, because carrying both items by hand would force two trips, and the תורה requires a single הבאה.

steps.title: Another way to avoid a spoon: incense in the hands, coal pan on top
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the כהן גדול could hold the קטורת in his cupped hands, rest the מחתה on top of his hands, and walk in. That would be one single trip without a spoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him take the incense in his handfuls, place the coal pan on top of it, and go in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes another way to bring the coals and the incense together in one trip without using a spoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said a spoon is needed because the כהן גדול may not make two trips. This suggestion meets that rule a different way: the incense stays in his hands, and the מחתה rests on top. If this works, the spoon is still unnecessary.

phrases.english: Let him take the incense in his handfuls
and place the coal pan on top of it
phrases.notes: The coal pan rests on top of his cupped hands.

phrases.english: and go in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new way to bring everything in one trip, testing the answer of Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 6 that a spoon is the only option
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One trip can be done without a spoon by stacking the מחתה on top of the handfuls of incense.

steps.title: Answer: he would have to use his teeth, which is disrespectful
steps.stepSummary: Once inside, the כהן גדול could only put down the מחתה by holding it in his teeth. One would not act that way before a human king, and all the more so before הקב"ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he gets there, what will he do? Take the coal pan in his teeth and lower it? Even before a human king people do not act that way. All the more so before the King of kings, הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion in Step 7. Once inside, there is no respectful way to put the pan down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His hands are full of incense, so his only way to set down the מחתה would be with his mouth. The גמרא uses a קל וחומר: if this is improper before a human king, it is certainly improper in the קודש הקדשים before הקב"ה.

keyTerms.meaning: A human king (a king of flesh and blood)
All the more so (a קל וחומר phrase)

phrases.english: When he arrives there, what should he do?
Should he take the coal pan in his teeth and lower it?
Now, before a king of flesh and blood
one does not act this way,
before the King of kings
the Holy One, Blessed be He —
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion of holding the incense in his hands with the מחתה on top
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no respectful way to put down the מחתה inside. Using his teeth is a disgrace before הקב"ה.

steps.title: No other way, so we follow the model of the נשיאים
steps.stepSummary: Since no other method works, the כהן גדול uses a spoon, as the נשיאים did when they brought incense in a golden כף at the dedication of the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, it is impossible any other way. Since it is impossible, we do as we find with the נשיאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes the discussion: the spoon is needed, and there is a precedent for it in the offerings of the נשיאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every way to avoid the spoon failed: two trips are not allowed, and using his teeth is disrespectful. So the גמרא adopts the method found in the תורה, where each נשיא brought "one golden spoon full of incense."

keyTerms.meaning: The tribal princes who brought offerings at the dedication of the משכן

steps.whatToRemember: The כף is used for the קטורת because there is no other respectful way to bring the coals and the incense in one trip. The source for using a spoon is the offering of the נשיאים.

phrases.english: Therefore, it is impossible,
and since it is impossible —
we act as we find with the princes.
phrases.notes: See במדבר ז:יד, "one golden spoon of ten shekels full of incense."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole question of Step 5 after the last alternative was rejected in Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כהן גדול must use a כף for the קטורת, following the precedent of the נשיאים.

steps.title: Why does the less important coal pan get the right hand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the מחתה is in the right hand and the כף in the left. It objects with a saying: "The native is on the ground and the stranger is in the highest heavens." The main item, the incense, should get the honored right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took the coal pan in his right hand and the spoon in his left. The native stays on the ground and the stranger is in the highest heavens!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. It immediately challenges the arrangement as backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main מצוה is the קטורת. The coals are only there to burn it. So the incense should get the more important right hand, yet the משנה gives the right hand to the coals. That is like honoring a guest above the person who lives there.

keyTerms.meaning: The native or permanent resident (here, the main item)
The stranger or newcomer (here, the secondary item)

steps.confusionAlert: "יציבא" and "גיורא" are not people in this case. This is a popular saying for an arrangement that seems upside down. The "native" is the incense (the main thing), and the "stranger" is the coal pan (the side item).

phrases.english: He took the coal pan in his right hand
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: and the spoon in his left.
The native is on the ground
and the stranger is in the highest heavens!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה, about which hand holds which vessel.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling: מחתה in the right hand, כף in the left
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The main item (the קטורת) should get the honored right hand, not the secondary item (the coals).

steps.title: The coal pan is heavier
steps.stepSummary: The מחתה full of coals is heavy, and the כף of incense is light. So the heavier load goes in the stronger right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (the coal pan) is heavy, and that one (the spoon) is light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of Step 10. The choice of hands is practical, not about honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right hand is the stronger hand, so it carries the heavier מחתה. This is about carrying safely, not about which item is more important.

phrases.english: This one is greater, and that one is less.
phrases.notes: The coal pan is heavier, and the spoon of incense is lighter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason replaces the honor reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hands should be assigned by importance, so the incense should be in the right hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hands are assigned by weight, so the heavier מחתה goes in the right hand.

steps.title: Even when the weights are equal, the coal pan is hot
steps.stepSummary: Even in a case like רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית, whose huge handfuls made the incense as heavy as the coals, the מחתה still goes in the right hand because it is hot and must be held carefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when the two are equal, as in the story of רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית, this one is hot and that one is cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its answer for a case where the weight reason does not apply, and gives a second practical reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית had very large hands, so his handfuls of incense could weigh as much as the coal pan. Even then, the right hand takes the מחתה because hot coals need the steadier, more careful hand.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול known for having very large hands

steps.whatToRemember: The מחתה is held in the right hand for practical reasons. It is heavier, and even when the weights are equal, it is hot.

phrases.english: And even when the two of them are equal,
as in the incident of Rabbi Yishmael ben Kimḥit,
phrases.notes: His handfuls were unusually large, so the incense could weigh as much as the coal pan.

phrases.english: this one is hot, and that one is cold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the answer of Step 11 to a case where the weights are equal.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional practical reason covering an edge case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When the weights are equal, the weight reason no longer applies, so perhaps the incense should get the right hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even then, the hot מחתה needs the right hand.

steps.title: The giant handfuls of רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית could scoop four קבין in his hands. He said his mother's 'selection' was better than all other women's.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית that he could scoop four קבין in his two handfuls. He would say: 'All women made selections, but my mother's selection rose up to the roof.'
steps.whatsHappening: Step 12 mentioned רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית, so the גמרא now tells more about him. It starts with his unusually huge hands and his explanation for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the case from step 12. His handfuls were so big that the קטורת could weigh as much as the coals. His saying means that his mother 'chose' something special, and that is why he grew so tall and large.

keyTerms.meaning: קבים, a measure of volume. Four of them is an enormous amount for two hands
A selection, or choosing the best (from a word for a choice young branch)
Rose up to the roof, meaning it reached the very top

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן קִמְחִית
phrases.english: They said about him, about Rabbi Yishmael ben Kimchis,
that he would scoop four kav
phrases.notes: This explains how his handful of incense could be as heavy as the coals (step 12).

phrases.english: in his full handfuls,
and he would say: All the women made selections,
but my mother's selection rose up to the roof.
phrases.notes: He is speaking about himself: his mother 'chose' the best, so he grew very large.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן קִמְחִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the figure mentioned in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית had enormous hands and credited his size to his mother's 'selection'

steps.title: First explanation: his mother ate fine flour
steps.stepSummary: One opinion says his mother 'selected' עַרְסָן, a healthful flour, based on רבי יחיאל's teaching that עַרְסָן is good for the sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the 'selection' was עַרְסָן, a kind of flour. This fits what רבה בר יונתן said in the name of רבי יחיאל: עַרְסָן is good for a sick person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what his mother 'selected.' The first opinion says it was a nourishing flour she ate while she was pregnant with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His saying was unclear, so the גמרא explains it. A food that is healthy enough to help the sick could also help an unborn child grow strong. That is why her son grew so large.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of fine, nourishing flour or porridge

phrases.english: Some say: it was a selection of fine flour,
in line with Rabba bar Yonatan.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יוֹנָתָן אָמַר רַבִּי יְחִיאֵל:
phrases.english: As Rabba bar Yonatan said that Rabbi Yechiel said:
Fine flour is good for the sick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the unclear word זרד from step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'selection' was עַרְסָן, a healthful flour, which is supported by רבי יחיאל's statement

steps.title: Second explanation: the selection was the best seed
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says the 'selection' refers to the זרע from which he was formed. It supports this from רבי אבהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say the 'selection' refers to the seed (שכבת זרע), in line with רבי אבהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of his mother's 'selection.' This is a setup line. The next steps bring רבי אבהו's teaching that backs it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word זרד is read as hinting at זרע: the best drop was chosen to form him. The גמרא does not prove this yet. It only points to רבי אבהו, whose teaching comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Seed. Here it means the drop from which a child is formed
And in line with (the view of)

phrases.english: And some say it refers to the seed,
in line with Rabbi Abbahu.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation that competes with step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'selection' refers to the choice seed from which he was formed

steps.title: Two verses about David use different words
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו points out that two parallel פסוקים about דוד use different words: וַתַּזְרֵנִי and הַמְאַזְּרֵנִי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו pointed out a contradiction. One פסוק says 'You girded me (וַתַּזְרֵנִי) with strength for battle,' and another says 'Who girds me (הַמְאַזְּרֵנִי) with strength.' Why the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings רבי אבהו's teaching. It starts with a question about why two nearly identical פסוקים use different spellings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same song of דוד appears in שמואל ב and in תהלים, but the key verb is spelled differently. רבי אבהו treats the difference as meaningful. That sets up an explanation in which one form hints at זרע.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a contradiction between two sources

phrases.english: For Rabbi Abbahu raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'You girded me with strength for battle,'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב כב:מ

phrases.english: and it is written: 'Who girds me with strength'?
phrases.notes: תהלים יח:לג. This is a parallel version of the same song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that step 15 pointed to
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference in wording between two parallel פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both פסוקים describe the same event, why does each use a different verb form?

steps.title: David: You selected me and shaped me
steps.stepSummary: The two words hint at two things: זֵרִיתַנִי (You selected me from the best seed) and זֵרַזְתַּנִי (You formed me well and made me strong).
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said before הקב"ה: 'Master of the World! You selected me (זֵרִיתַנִי) and You made me strong (זֵרַזְתַּנִי).'
steps.whatsHappening: This answers רבי אבהו's question. Each spelling hints at a different thing הקב"ה did for דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זֵרִיתַנִי means הקב"ה chose the best drop of זרע to form דוד. זֵרַזְתַּנִי means He made him strong and energetic. This supports the second opinion: a person's great size or strength can come from the choice זרע he was formed from, as with רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית.

keyTerms.meaning: You selected (or 'sifted') me, from the best seed
You made me strong and energetic

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of the 'selection' that made רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית so large. Either his mother ate עַרְסָן, a healthful flour, or he was formed from choice זרע, as רבי אבהו teaches about דוד.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe!
You selected me and You made me strong.
phrases.notes: Each spelling in the two verses hints at one of these two ideas.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both wordings are kept, and each one adds its own meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two spellings are just different ways of saying 'girded'
steps.terutzMaskana: One form hints at being selected from choice זרע, and the other at being made strong

steps.title: Saliva from an Arab: ישבב serves instead
steps.stepSummary: On יום הכפורים, saliva from an Arab landed on רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית's clothes and made him טמא. His brother ישבב served as כהן גדול in his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית: once he was talking with an Arab in the market, and a drop of saliva sprayed from the Arab's mouth onto his clothes. His brother ישבב went in and served in his place. Their mother saw two sons serve as כהן גדול on one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story about רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית. Because he became טמא, he could not do the עבודה, so his brother replaced him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By rabbinic law, a non-Jew's saliva is treated like the saliva of a זב, so it makes the person it touches טמא. Since the כהן גדול was now unable to serve, a replacement took over. As a result, one mother had two sons serve as כהן גדול on the same day.
steps.confusionAlert: The word מִפִּיו ('from his mouth') means the Arab's mouth, not רבי ישמעאל's. The saliva came from the non-Jew, and that is what made the כהן גדול טמא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן קִמְחִית:
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Yishmael ben Kimchis:
Once he was conversing
with a certain Arab in the market,
and a drop of saliva sprayed from his (the Arab's) mouth onto his (Rabbi Yishmael's) clothes.
phrases.notes: The saliva made him rabbinically טמא, like a זב's saliva.

phrases.english: And his brother Yeshevav entered and served in his place.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָאֲתָה אִמָּן שְׁנֵי כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים בְּיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: And their mother saw two High Priests in one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן קִמְחִית: פַּעַם אַחַת סִיפֵּר דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about the same person
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-Jew's saliva made the כהן גדול טמא, so his brother ישבב replaced him

steps.title: Saliva from an officer: יוסף serves instead
steps.stepSummary: A second, parallel story: saliva from a הגמון (officer) made him טמא, and his brother יוסף served in his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also said about him: once he went out and talked with an officer in the market, and a drop of saliva sprayed from the officer's mouth onto his clothes. His brother יוסף went in and served in his place. Again, their mother saw two sons serve as כהן גדול on one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story that follows almost the same pattern as the first. Only the people change: an officer instead of an Arab, and the brother יוסף instead of ישבב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated story shows this happened more than once. It also shows how a single drop of saliva from a non-Jew could disqualify the כהן גדול. Each time, a different brother took his place.
steps.whatToRemember: These two stories are almost identical. Both times a non-Jew's saliva made רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית טמא, and a brother (first ישבב, then יוסף) served as כהן גדול instead. So their mother twice saw two sons serve on the same day.

phrases.aramaic: וְשׁוּב אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן קִמְחִית:
phrases.english: And they further said about Rabbi Yishmael ben Kimchis:
Once he went out and conversed
with a certain officer in the market,
and a drop of saliva sprayed from his (the officer's) mouth onto his clothes.
and his brother Yosef entered and served in his place,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets (עִם), so the line simply reads 'his brother יוסף.'

phrases.aramaic: וְרָאֲתָה אִמָּן שְׁנֵי כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים בְּיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and their mother saw two High Priests in one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוּב אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן קִמְחִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second time, a non-Jew's saliva made him טמא, and his brother יוסף replaced him

steps.title: קמחית's seven sons and the reason she gave
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says קמחית had seven sons who all served as כהן גדול. When the Sages asked how she earned this, she said the beams of her house never saw her hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: קמחית had seven sons, and all of them served as כהן גדול. The Sages asked her, 'What did you do to deserve this?' She answered, 'In all my days, the beams of my house never saw the braids of my hair.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story of רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית from Steps 18–19 with a ברייתא about his mother. She explains that she earned her sons' greatness through extreme modesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 18–19 showed brothers stepping in as כהן גדול when רבי ישמעאל became טמא. This ברייתא widens the picture: all seven of her sons served in that role. She points to her own conduct: she kept her hair covered even inside her own home, where no one could see.

keyTerms.meaning: The mother of רבי ישמעאל בן קמחית and his brothers
The office of the כהן גדול (High Priest)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Kimchit had seven sons,
and all of them served as High Priest.
The Sages said to her:
What did you do that you merited this?
She said to them:
In all my days, the beams of my house never saw
phrases.notes: Even inside her own home, where no person could see, she kept her hair covered.

phrases.english: the braids of my hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁבְעָה בָּנִים הָיוּ לָהּ לְקִמְחִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the story of the קמחית brothers from Steps 18–19 to the whole family.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All seven of קמחית's sons served as כהן גדול, and she credited this to her extreme modesty.

steps.title: The Sages answer that modesty alone does not explain it
steps.stepSummary: The Sages tell her that many women acted the same way and did not get this reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to her: 'Many women did the same, and it did not bring them this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages push back on her explanation. Many women were just as modest, so modesty alone cannot explain such a rare result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her reason is not rejected as a good deed. It is rejected as a full explanation. If the same behavior did not produce the same result for other women, her reward must be a special gift from Heaven beyond the normal measure.

keyTerms.meaning: And it did not help them / they did not succeed

steps.confusionAlert: The Sages are not saying her modesty was worthless. They are saying it cannot be the whole reason, since others did the same without this result.

phrases.english: They said to her:
Many did so and it did not help them.

steps.whatToRemember: קמחית credited her modesty, but the Sages said her reward went beyond what such conduct normally brings. It was a special gift.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהּ: הַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ כֵּן וְלֹא הוֹעִילוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to and limits קמחית's explanation from Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects modesty as a complete explanation for her reward, not the value of modesty itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same conduct by many other women did not produce the same result.

steps.title: The קומץ of a מנחה must be taken by hand
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'בקומצו' (with his handful) that the קומץ may not be measured with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'בקומצו' (with his handful) teaches that he may not make a measuring tool for the קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new halachic topic. It quotes a ברייתא saying that the כהן must take the קומץ of a מנחה with his own hand, not with a measuring vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בקומצו' points to his own hand. So the amount is fixed by the actual hand of the כהן, and a cup or scoop cannot replace it. This rule is the starting point for the question that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: With his handful (pinched closed fingers), the word in the פסוק about the מנחה
The handful removed from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'With his handful' —
that he should not make a measure (vessel) for the handful.

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule about the מנחה is the model for the question about the קטורת that follows.
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּקוּמְצוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה מִדָּה לַקּוֹמֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The story of קמחית is finished, and the גמרא returns to the עבודה of the day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קומץ of a מנחה must be taken with the hand itself, not measured with a vessel.

steps.title: Does the same rule apply to the incense handful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the כהן גדול may use a measuring vessel for the חפינה of קטורת on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: may he make a measuring tool for the חפינה (the double handful of incense)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question. Does the 'no measuring tool' rule for the מנחה also apply to the incense handful on יום הכפורים? This line sets up the next step, where both sides are explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול takes a double handful (חפינה) of קטורת to bring into the קודש הקדשים. The question is whether that amount must come from his actual hands, like the קומץ, or whether a vessel of that size could be used.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real halachic doubt)
Taking a double handful (both hands cupped), used for the קטורת

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
May he make a measure (vessel) for the double handful?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה מִדָּה לַחֲפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the rule from Step 22 extends to the קטורת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חפינה of קטורת may be measured with a vessel, or must be taken by hand like the קומץ.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the rule only applies to the מנחה, because only there does the פסוק say 'בקומצו'. Or maybe the word 'מלא' links the two cases, so the same rule applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, by the מנחה, it is written 'בקומצו' (with his handful). But here it does not say 'בחפניו' (with his hands). It says 'מלא חפניו קטורת סמים דקה' (his hands full of fine incense), so perhaps the rule does not apply. Or perhaps he learns 'מלא' from 'מלא' and connects it to 'קומצו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard. Each side of the question has a reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: 'בקומצו' clearly requires the hand. 'מלא חפניו' may only be describing an amount, a handful's worth, which a vessel could also hold. Side two: the word 'מלא' appears in both sections. Through a word link, the hand requirement of the קומץ carries over to the קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: His hands full, from the פסוק about the קטורת on יום הכפורים
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: Side one does not say the קטורת needs no hands at all. It says the פסוק may only be giving a size, so a vessel of that size might be acceptable.

phrases.english: There it is that it is written 'with his handful';
but here, where it is not written 'with his hands,'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: ״מְלֹא חׇפְנָיו קְטוֹרֶת סַמִּים דַּקָּה״, לָא.
phrases.english: but rather 'his hands full of fine sweet incense' — no (the rule does not apply).
phrases.notes: ויקרא ט״ז:י״ב

phrases.english: Or perhaps he learns 'full' from 'full' from 'his handful'?
phrases.notes: The word 'מלא' also appears in the context of the קומץ (ויקרא ב׳:ב׳), which creates the link.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the reasoning behind both sides of the question from Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the פסוק's wording 'מלא חפניו' only give a size, or does the word link 'מלא'–'מלא' require the hands, as with the קומץ?

steps.title: A proof from the משנה's words 'this was its measure'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'וכך היתה מדתה' in the משנה means he could also use a different measure, such as a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And this was its measure.' Doesn't that mean that if he wanted to use a different measure, he could?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from the wording of the משנה. 'This was its measure' sounds like the handful is just one possible way of measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof reads 'וכך היתה מדתה' as describing the usual practice, not a requirement. If the hand were required, the משנה would not need to call it 'its measure'. So a vessel would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: And this was its measure (words from the משנה)
Is it not that (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And this was its measure.'
Is it not (to say)

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם רָצָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מִדָּה אַחֶרֶת עוֹשֶׂה?
phrases.english: that if he wanted to make a different measure, he may do so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from Steps 23–24 using the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a measuring vessel may be used for the חפינה.

steps.title: The proof is rejected: it describes scooping again inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה means that he would scoop the same incense again in the same way inside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. This is what it means: and in this same way he would scoop it again inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. 'This was its measure' is not about using a different tool. It describes him scooping the incense again inside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is reread. It means the same handful taken outside is scooped again by hand inside, before being placed on the coals. Once it is read this way, the משנה says nothing about whether a vessel may be used, so the question is not yet answered.

phrases.english: No, this is what it is saying:
and in this same way he would scoop it again inside.

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether a vessel may measure the קטורת handful stays open. The proof from 'וכך היתה מדתה' fails, because those words describe him scooping again inside.
steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, הָכִי קָאָמַר: וְכָךְ הָיָה חוֹזֵר וְחוֹפְנָהּ לִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 25 by rereading the משנה's words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. The question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'וכך היתה מדתה' refers to scooping the same incense again inside, not to permitting a different measure.

steps.title: So the High Priest scoops twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds on the last reading of the משנה. If 'וכך היתה מדתה' means he scooped the same way again inside the קודש הקדשים, then the משנה proves the debated rule that he scoops a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is what the משנה means, then we learn from it that the כהן גדול scoops, and then scoops again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the reading it just gave the משנה and uses it to try to settle a different debate. The debate is whether the כהן גדול scoops the קטורת a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the גמרא said the משנה means he measured the same scoop again inside the קודש הקדשים. If so, the משנה is describing a second scooping. That would settle a separate argument, discussed later, about whether there really is a second חפינה.

keyTerms.meaning: You can learn from this; a phrase that introduces a proof drawn from what was just said
He scoops with both hands (cupped hands)
And he goes back and scoops again

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same question as steps 23-26. Those steps asked whether he may use a measuring vessel. Here the גמרא uses the answer from step 26 to try to settle a second question: does he scoop twice?

phrases.english: You can learn from this:
he scoops, and then scoops again!
phrases.notes: This means a second scooping inside the קודש הקדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reading of the משנה from step 26 to try to settle a separate question about scooping twice.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the כהן גדול scoops the קטורת a second time inside the קודש הקדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'וכך היתה מדתה', read as in step 26

steps.title: The משנה can be read other ways, so nothing is proven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe the משנה means he may measure with a vessel if he wants. Or maybe it means he must take exactly the right amount, no less and no more. Neither reading says anything about a second scooping.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה means that if he wants to measure the amount, he may do so. Or else it means that he must not take less and must not take more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof in step 27. It offers two other possible meanings for 'וכך היתה מדתה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first option brings back the reading from step 25: he may use a measuring vessel. The second option says the words only teach precision: exactly two handfuls, no less and no more. Since the משנה has more than one possible meaning, it cannot prove that he scoops twice. The vessel question also stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; a word the גמרא uses to begin pushing back on a proof
A measure; here, measuring with a vessel
That he not take less and not take more

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'וכך היתה מדתה' has three possible readings, and the גמרא does not decide between them. (1) He may measure with a vessel. (2) He scoops the same way again inside. (3) He must take an exact amount. So neither the vessel question nor the second-scooping question is settled from here.

phrases.english: Perhaps it means: that if he wanted
to make a measure, he may do so.
phrases.notes: This means measuring with a vessel, the reading from step 25.

phrases.english: Alternatively: that he must not take less
and must not take more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 27 by showing the משנה's words have other possible meanings.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה, both for scooping twice and as a firm answer to the vessel question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes only one reading of 'וכך היתה מדתה'. But the phrase can also mean measuring with a vessel, or simply taking an exact amount.

steps.title: How a proper handful is taken
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses two phrases from the פסוקים to define the קומץ. 'בקומצו' rules out an overflowing handful. 'מלא קומצו' rules out using only the fingertips. In practice, he closes three fingers over his palm and takes the handful.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: the פסוק says 'a full handful.' You might think the hand should be heaped and overflowing. So the פסוק says 'with his handful,' meaning an exact handful. But if it only said 'with his handful,' you might think even the fingertips are enough. So the פסוק says 'a full handful,' meaning the way people normally take a handful. How is it done? He closes his three fingers over the palm of his hand and takes the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that explains exactly what a proper קומץ of a מנחה looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase in the פסוקים blocks a mistake the other phrase could lead to. 'מלא' by itself could suggest an overflowing heap, so 'בקומצו' limits it to an exact handful. 'בקומצו' by itself could allow a tiny fingertip pinch, so 'מלא' requires a full, normal handful. The result is a middle point: three fingers closed over the palm.

keyTerms.meaning: Overflowing; heaped up beyond the hand
Therefore the פסוק says; this introduces the word that settles the question
The way people normally take a handful

steps.whatToRemember: A proper קומץ is a normal, full handful: three fingers closed over the palm. It is not a heaped, overflowing handful, and not a fingertip pinch.
steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases come from two different פסוקים: 'מלא קומצו' is in ויקרא ב:ב and 'בקומצו' is in ויקרא ו:ח. They work together, each one limiting the other. The word 'מלא' is not being thrown out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical way the קמיצה of every מנחה is performed. It also gives the background for comparing the קומץ to the חפינה of the קטורת through the word 'מלא'.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: 'His full handful.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ב:ב

phrases.english: I might think it should be overflowing,
therefore the verse says: 'With his handful.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ו:ח. This means an exact handful.

phrases.english: If it said only 'with his handful,'
I might think even with just his fingertips,
therefore the verse says: 'His full handful,'
the way people normally take a handful.
So how is it done?
He closes his three fingers
over the palm of his hand and takes the handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a ברייתא that defines how the קומץ itself is physically taken.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קומץ must be a normal, full handful, taken by closing three fingers over the palm. It may not be overflowing, and it may not be only a fingertip pinch.
